summary: Hyoung Seok Ham is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Korea University, the University of Virginia, and the University of Michigan (PhD circa 2009–2016), where his doctoral supervisor was Madhav M. Deshpande.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in religious, Buddhist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge (circa 2000–2005), held a post there (circa 2004–2012), and became a professor at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōkai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.
Hōkei Izumi (1884–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University until circa 1910 and later served as a professor there from circa 1923 to 1944.

Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge and Lancaster. He founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies and held posts at Lancaster, Oxford, the Becket Institute, Singapore, and Cumbria (Professor Emeritus).

Ian James Coghlan is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University in 2004. He served as a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute, Monash University.
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka. He taught Shunryu Suzuki.

Ian Reader (born 1949) is a Japanology and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Leeds (circa 1979–1983). He held posts at Kansai Gaidai, Stirling, Hawaii, Lancaster, and the University of Hyogo.

Ibrahim Shah specializes in history and archaeology. He completed a PhD in Archaeology at the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Muhammad Farooq Swati and became an associate professor and department chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Otani University (circa 1955–1959). He held posts at Otani University Junior College starting in 1974 and Otani University in 1987.

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1932–1935). He held posts at Kokugakuin, Tohoku, the University of Tokyo, Seijo University, and Nishogakusha University.
Ichiro Katayama (born 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University from circa 1961 to 1965 and served as a professor there from circa 1993 to 2013.
Ichiro Kominami (born 1942) is a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1961 to 1965. He held an academic post at Ryukoku University from circa 2005 to 2012.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome until circa 1864 and held a post there from circa 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1936–1941), he held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, Pravda, and the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Oriental Studies.
Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University in 2004 under MA supervisor Shiro Matsumoto. He served as a part-time lecturer at Komazawa University.

Ikuhisa Takigawa (born 1968) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He has held positions as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki works in Buddhist and religious studies. Her academic appointments include serving as a special researcher at Otani University and as a collaborative researcher at Kyoto University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki in 1993 under René Gothóni. He became an Academy Research Fellow at Helsinki in 1984 and visited Oxford in 2007.

Imre Galambos (born 1967) is a Sinologist and Tibetologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd, Nankai, and UC Berkeley (PhD 2002). He held posts at UC Santa Barbara, the British Library, Ryukoku University, and Cambridge (2012).
